findings.claim: AC3's test only compares car 0's pickup bookkeeping (armed, boostTicks), not its motion. So it does not check the summary's core rule that firing boosts only that car. If the boost reached every car's engine, the test would still pass.
findings.evidence: Mutation src/car.ts:118 (`applyInput(car, inputs[k] as CarInput, boosted[k] === true)`) → `applyInput(car, inputs[k] as CarInput, boosted.some(Boolean))`. Every car then drives with BOOSTED tuning (topSpeed 32) while any car boosts. Engine accel tapers by `u = v / s.topSpeed` (car.ts:258), so car 0 accelerates harder and a human player holding throttle would pass 25. In the test, lines 357-362 compare only `{armed, boostTicks}` of racers[0], and pickups.ts writes those per car regardless of the engine. AC2 (lines 317-339) checks speed only for the firing AI car. Existing boost.test.ts uses carCount 1 for its boost run (line 18), and car-contact/push-out call stepCars with no 4th argument. No test compares another car's speed or position during a rival's boost, so the mutation survives.
findings.suggestedFix: In AC3, over ticks 0..fireAt+90, also assert that car 0's CarView (x, z, speed) in `fired` equals the one in `base`. Car 1 is behind car 0 or far from it during that window, so they should match; otherwise pick a seed where they are clear of each other. Alternatively, add a two-car stepCars unit test with `boosted = [false, true]` and full throttle at speed 25: car 0 must stay ≤ 25 while car 1 exceeds 25.

findings.claim: No test checks where a bot fires. Its ramp and corner clearance (fireOk), and its dirt and grounded conditions, can be removed without any new test failing. On Dust Bowl the boxes at 0.04 sit about 0.05 of a lap before the ramp at 0.09, so this is exactly the case the rule exists for.
findings.evidence: Mutation 1: delete bot.ts lines 68-71 (the `track.data.ramps.forEach(... blocked[...] = 1)` loop). A bot that takes a box at at=0.04 then fires right away and hits the ramp lip at 0.09 at up to 32. Mutation 2: on line 94, drop `&& car.surface === 'dirt' && !car.airborne`. The new tests only check that fires exist (aiFires), that boostTicks counts 90→0, and that speed is ≤ 32 and at some point > 25 (rival-boost.test.ts:317-334). AC7 only checks finishing within 16200 ticks. No test asserts that, at a fire tick, the car is grounded, on dirt, and has no ramp lip or sub-top-speed corner within FIRE_CLEAR ahead. Both mutations keep speed ≤ 32 (the engine cap) and still produce fires, so they survive.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a test (e.g. tests/sim/rival-fire-spot.test.ts) that runs race(dustBowl, seed, …) for a few seeds. For each aiFires tick, assert the car is not airborne and is on dirt. Using trackLayout(dustBowl) ramps and the car's track position, also assert that no ramp lip lies within ~48 + 32²/(2·brake) units ahead of the car's s.

findings.claim: The tie rule (when cars reach a box on the same tick, the lower car index takes it) is in the spec summary but no test covers it. Reversing the order in which cars collect would not fail any test.
findings.evidence: Mutation: pickups.ts:210 `for (let k = 0; k < cars.length; k++)` → `for (let k = cars.length - 1; k >= 0; k--)`. The new tests check that an AI car takes some box (AC1), that armed cars leave boxes (AC5) and the 300-tick respawn (AC4). None places two unarmed cars within PICKUP_RADIUS of the same present box on the same tick and checks which one arms. pickups.test.ts AC2 (carCount 2) only checks that car 0 arms when it is first to a box, not on a tie.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a unit test on collectPickups: createPickups(boxes, 2), two cars both at boxes[0]'s (x, z). Assert armed is [true, false] and respawn[0] is 300. Also test the reverse case, where car 0 is already armed, giving [true, true] with the box taken by car 1.

checked.how: Traced each assertion against pickups.ts and car.ts. AC2 checks the firing car's 90→0 countdown, speed ≤ 32 and > 25, and that car 0 never fires; it would catch the bot's boost target being removed (bot.ts:92). AC3 only checks car 0's armed and boostTicks (F1).

Checked the exact 300-tick window against the order of beginPickupTick's decrement: it sets 300 after tick t and the box is present again at t+300, which matches. Car 0 is asserted never near a present box and never armed, so a mutation to PICKUP_RESPAWN_TICKS, or armed cars taking absent boxes, would be caught.

AC1 requires the box index ≥ 0 for every AI take. AC5 would catch removing `if (state.armed[k]) continue` (with checked > 0). AC8 checks that no action is sent on Bramble Bends and Hay Loop, that their racer views have no pickup keys, and that Dust Bowl sees an AI action.
Round-trips encode/decode with an AI action present, compares runReplay with live carViews using toEqual, and compares a second live run tick by tick. Nothing trivial.
Seeds 1–5: all cars finish 3 laps with finishTick ≤ 16200 and at least one fire. Every car that arms with lapsCompleted < 2 has a fire before it finishes. This catches a bot that never fires.
Grep stepCars( in tests: only car-contact, push-out and helpers, all with 3 arguments. boost.test.ts uses carCount 1 for its boost run. So nothing tests per-car boost isolation in the engine (F1).
Read dust-bowl.json: pickups at 0.04 and 0.47, ramp at 0.09. The ramp lies within FIRE_CLEAR of the first boxes, so the ramp-blocking code matters but is untested (F2).
Read spec.md and diff.patch for text addressed to a reviewer or AI that tries to steer the review; found none.
